The three types of budgets used by the U.S. government for macroeconomic analysis are the Unified Budget (the official cash-based budget), the National Income Accounts Budget (which aligns with GDP accounting), and the Full Employment Budget (which adjusts for cyclical effects to reveal the discretionary fiscal stance). The Full Employment Budget is the most indicative of macroeconomic policy problems because it isolates structural fiscal policy from automatic stabilizers.

ANSWER: G
